title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.
intro: This training programme equips new entrants to the funds industry and its supervisors with a complete grounding in how investment funds are organised, regulated, governed, operated and wound up.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give participants a structured, end-to-end understanding of investment funds, from first principles through organisation, legal form, regulation, governance, fund types, distribution, documentation, operations, investment, legal matters and the fund lifecycle. Participants leave able to follow how each party contributes to a fund and to speak confidently with managers, service providers, investors and supervisors.
sections.What It Covers: What funds are and why investors use them, the parties to a fund, legal forms and structures, regulation of funds and managers, governance and delegation, traditional and alternative fund types, marketing and distribution, fund documentation, dealing, pricing and liquidity, portfolio investment, legal considerations and the lifecycle from launch to wind-down.
Intended Audience: New joiners and graduates at fund managers, administrators, depositaries, transfer agents, law firms and distributors
Staff of supervisory authorities joining fund supervision or authorisation teams
Professionals moving into the funds industry from banking, audit or other sectors who need a complete foundation
Learning Objectives: Explain what an investment fund is, how it works and why different investors use funds
Describe the roles of the management company, investment manager, depositary, administrator and other parties
Compare the main legal forms and structures a fund can take and the reasons for choosing each
Outline how funds, managers and their distribution are regulated and how fund governance and delegation work
Distinguish traditional, money market, exchange traded and alternative funds and the documentation each produces
Follow a fund's operations, investments, legal arrangements and risks across its lifecycle from launch to termination
sections.Structure and Format: Fourteen modules of around three hours each, deliverable as a two-week foundation course, a series of half-day sessions or a blended online programme. Each module combines short teaching inputs, worked examples using real fund documents and knowledge checks, and modules can be selected or tailored to a firm's or authority's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of investment funds is required. A general awareness of financial markets is helpful.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2013), Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes
IOSCO (2018), Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes
FSB (2017), Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Asset Management Activities

modules.title: What Investment Funds Are and How They Work
modules.summary: The basic idea of pooled investment, how a fund turns investors' money into a managed portfolio, and why investors choose funds over direct investment.
objectives: Describe an investment fund and the pooling of investor money
Explain the benefits of diversification, professional management and scale
Identify the main types of investor and how they access funds
syllabus: Pooled investment, units, shares and net asset value
Why investors subscribe: diversification, expertise, liquidity and cost
Retail, professional and institutional investors
Access routes: direct, platforms, advisers and wrappers

modules.title: The Parties to an Investment Fund
modules.summary: Who does what in a fund, from the management company and investment manager to the depositary, administrator and the wider circle of service providers.
objectives: Describe the roles of the management company and investment manager
Explain the safekeeping, oversight and administration functions
Identify the other parties involved and how they connect
syllabus: How a fund is organised and the flow of responsibilities
Management company and investment manager
Depositary and fund administrator: custody, oversight, valuation and transfer agency
Distributors, auditors, legal advisers, brokers and other parties

modules.title: Legal Forms of Investment Funds
modules.summary: The four main legal forms a fund can take, how each holds assets and treats investors, and why a sponsor would choose one over another.
objectives: Describe corporate funds, unit trusts, contractual funds and limited partnerships
Explain how legal form affects investor rights, governance and tax
Assess the rationale for choosing a particular legal form
syllabus: Corporate investment funds and the role of shareholders
Unit trusts and the trustee relationship
Contractual funds and co-ownership models
Limited partnerships: general and limited partners

modules.title: Fund Structures: Stand-Alone, Umbrella and Beyond
modules.summary: How funds are structured to share costs, offer choice and pool assets, and the advantages and drawbacks of each structure.
objectives: Explain stand-alone and umbrella structures and segregated liability
Describe fund of funds, multi-manager and master-feeder arrangements
Weigh the pros and cons of each structure for sponsors and investors
syllabus: Stand-alone funds and umbrella funds with sub-funds
Segregation of liability between sub-funds
Fund of funds and multi-manager structures
Master-feeder structures and their uses

modules.title: How Funds and Their Managers Are Regulated
modules.summary: What determines how a fund is regulated, the main types of fund and manager regime, and how investment services rules apply to distribution.
objectives: Identify the factors that determine a fund's regulatory treatment
Describe retail fund product rules and alternative fund manager regimes
Explain how investment services rules apply to fund distribution
syllabus: Fund domicile, investor type and legal form as regulatory drivers
Retail fund product regimes: eligible assets, diversification and investor protection
Alternative fund manager regimes and their requirements
Investment services rules, cross-border passports and international standards

modules.title: Governance and Oversight of Funds
modules.summary: How fund governance is structured, how management companies are organised, and how the board and key personnel oversee delegated activities.
objectives: Describe the governance structure of a fund and its management company
Explain the role of the fund board and its directors
Explain how key personnel and assurance functions oversee delegates
syllabus: Governance structure of an investment fund
Organisation and substance of management companies
Fund board composition, duties and independence
Key management personnel, assurance functions and delegate oversight

modules.title: Types of Investment Fund
modules.summary: The features that distinguish fund types, how funds are classified by regulators, and a closer look at exchange traded funds and money market funds.
objectives: Identify the factors that distinguish different types of fund
Describe regulatory classifications of retail and alternative funds
Explain how exchange traded funds and money market funds work
syllabus: Asset class, strategy, liquidity and investor type
Regulatory classification of funds
Exchange traded funds: creation, redemption and secondary trading
Money market funds: types, liquidity rules and stability

modules.title: Alternative Investment Funds
modules.summary: The main alternative fund types, how their strategies, liquidity and investor base differ, and the specialist fund labels used for long-term investment.
objectives: Describe hedge funds, private equity and real estate funds
Explain how loan origination funds work and their risks
Outline specialist and labelled long-term investment funds
syllabus: Hedge funds: strategies, leverage and liquidity terms
Private equity and loan origination funds
Real estate funds
Specialist alternative funds and long-term, venture and social investment fund labels

modules.title: Marketing and Distribution of Funds
modules.summary: How funds reach investors, how marketing is regulated, and how funds are sold across borders within and outside regional passport regimes.
objectives: Describe the channels used to market and distribute funds
Explain how fund marketing is regulated
Distinguish passported, private placement and third-country marketing routes
syllabus: Distribution channels, platforms and intermediaries
Regulation of fund marketing and communications
Cross-border marketing within a passport regime
Marketing outside the home region and private placement regimes

modules.title: Fund Documentation and Key Agreements
modules.summary: The prospectus, investor disclosures, promotional materials and the agreements that bind a fund to its manager and service providers.
objectives: Explain the purpose and content of a fund prospectus
Describe the documents investors receive and promotional materials
Outline the investment management agreement and service provider contracts
syllabus: The prospectus and supplements
Key information documents, reports and accounts for investors
Promotional materials and fair communication
Investment management, depositary, administration and distribution agreements

modules.title: Fund Operations: Dealing, Pricing and Liquidity
modules.summary: How investors subscribe and redeem, how funds are valued and priced, and how liquidity risk is managed day to day.
objectives: Explain the subscription and redemption process
Describe valuation, pricing and net asset value calculation
Explain liquidity risk management tools and other fund transactions
syllabus: Operational features that drive fund processes
Subscriptions, dealing cycles and investor onboarding
Valuation, pricing and net asset value calculation
Redemptions, liquidity management tools, switches and transfers

modules.title: Investing the Fund's Portfolio
modules.summary: What determines how a fund invests, the assets funds buy and sell, the rules that constrain portfolios and the techniques managers use.
objectives: Describe the investment considerations for a fund
Explain the main asset classes funds hold
Describe regulatory limits and investment techniques such as derivatives and leverage
syllabus: Investment objective, policy and restrictions
Equities, bonds, money market instruments, derivatives and real assets
Regulatory limits: eligible assets, diversification and leverage
Investment techniques: hedging, securities lending and efficient portfolio management

modules.title: Legal Considerations for Funds
modules.summary: The legal issues funds face, the role of legal counsel, ownership of fund assets, contracts and how security is taken and given over assets.
objectives: Describe the main legal issues for investment funds
Explain legal and beneficial ownership of fund assets
Explain contract law considerations and methods of taking security
syllabus: The legal issues for funds and the role of legal counsel
Legal and beneficial ownership
Contract law: formation, terms, liability and termination
Taking and providing security: pledges, charges, title transfer and collateral

modules.title: The Fund Lifecycle: Launch, Risk and Wind-Down
modules.summary: How a new fund is designed, authorised and launched, how risk is managed through its life, and how a fund is terminated and wound up.
objectives: Explain the considerations for establishing and authorising a new fund
Describe how risk is managed across the fund lifecycle
Explain how a fund is terminated, merged or wound up
syllabus: Product design, domicile choice and the authorisation process
Launch, seeding and bringing a fund to market
Risk management through the lifecycle: investment, liquidity, operational and counterparty
Workshop: closing, merging and winding up a fund

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Investment Funds Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment funds and their managers, from authorisation and valuation to liquidity, leverage, private markets and tokenised funds.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.
